newsitem.title: USA: Clinton agrees to expand broadcasts to China.
newsitem.headline: Clinton agrees to expand broadcasts to China.

text.p: President Clinton on Thursday agreed to step up U.S. radio broadcasts to China in an attempt to encourage members of Congress to support renewal of China's most-favoured-nation (MFN) trade status.
In a letter to Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Clinton termed it "critical" to promote a free exchange of ideas and information in the world's most populous country.
"I welcome your call for increased funding to expand U.S.- supported international broadcasting into China," Clinton said.
Gingrich made the appeal on Monday among recommendations on ways to influence China other than by extending MFN. He wants the United States to pursue a tougher policy toward China.
Clinton's letter to Gingrich was released in Denver, where the president is preparing to host a summit of the world's leading industrial nations.
Clinton has been an unabashed promoter of extending MFN to China, saying it is the best way to remain engaged with the communist giant.

"My administration has strongly supported broadcasts to China by both Radio Free Asia and Voice of America, and I believe there is more that each service could accomplish with A vote in Congress on Clinton's China trade policy is expected later this month. Congress could vote to overturn his decision to renew MFN but would need to muster a two-thirds majority to overcome a presidential veto.

The White House has waged a campaign to convince Congress that China should keep the tariff relief, arguing that engagement with Beijing offers the best opportunity for democratic reforms, human rights improvements and opening Chinese markets.
Clinton said he would work with Gingrich and others in Congress to obtain the money to provide 24 hours of Mandarin broadcasting daily to China and "appropriate broadcasting in other dialects."
